scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A bicycle falls over when it's still, but stays up when it's moving. Why is balancing easier at speed?

scenes.name: steer
scenes.text: The main trick is steering. When the bike leans left, you turn the wheel left, bringing the wheels back under you.

scenes.name: speed
scenes.text: At higher speed, a small steer quickly moves the wheels under your weight, so tiny corrections are enough.

scenes.name: trail
scenes.text: The front fork is angled, so the wheel touches the ground behind the steering line. When the bike tips, the wheel turns itself into the lean.

scenes.name: gyro
scenes.text: Spinning wheels help a little, through gyroscopic effects, but scientists found they aren't the main reason.

scenes.name: rider
scenes.text: Your brain constantly makes small steering and body adjustments, without you even thinking about it.

scenes.name: learn
scenes.text: That's why going a bit faster and looking ahead makes learning to ride much easier.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Steer into the fall, let speed help. Follow for more on how things really work.
